newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy judge rules no damages in smoking claim.
newsitem.headline: Italy judge rules no damages in smoking claim.

text.p: A judge ruled on Thursday that the family of an Italian smoker who died of lung cancer had no grounds for compensation from the state tobacco monopoly.

The widow and son of Mario Stalteri, who died of a lung tumour in 1991, had sought damages from the monopoly after they claimed that it had omitted for decades to inform consumers about the dangers of smoking.
Health warnings have appeared on cigarette packets in Italy only since 1989.

Judge Alberto Bucci ruled that the monopoly "had no legal obligation before 1989 to inform consumers about the risk of smoking". Stalteri "having voluntarily taken tobacco, had accepted the consequences of his choice", he said.

Lawyers for the Stalteri family referred to negotiations in the United States between tobacco industry executives and state attorneys general on a possible settlement of massive litigation against the industry, and said they would appeal the ruling.
"We are sure that other judges...will know how to confirm and defend a right which has found tangible recognition in the United States," they said in a statement.
U.S. lawyers and tobacco firms are discussing the establishment of a $300 billion fund to pay for smoking-related injuries over a 25-year period.
